_comment: QUARANTINED. My prior read of which approach is stronger and why, written when the forks were designed. It is NOT gold and NOT an answer key — the design does not depend on one plan being wrong, only on the two being distinct. Generators independently repaired most of the weaknesses I anticipated (see REPORT-NOTES.md Note 2), so treat this as a record of intent rather than a prediction. Never shown to a generator or evaluator; used only to compare against the human gold once it exists.

intent.S1: M1 stronger. M2 is mechanically circular: DraftKings spend sits in the denominator of the share variable, so a fall in DraftKings raises Kalshi share by construction and the coefficient is guaranteed negative with no substitution occurring. This is the trap — share-of-wallet framing is standard and reads sophisticated.
intent.S2: M1 stronger. M2 is the Part 0 flawed plan: log-levels with FE leaves common trend intact, a random company-quarter holdout trains on future to predict past, and a 3% MAPE bar is clearable by persistence alone since ARR is heavily autocorrelated. It succeeds on its own terms, which is what makes it dangerous.
intent.S3: M1 stronger. M2's validation is circular — silhouette, bootstrap stability and cross-window agreement all measure whether the SAME features cluster consistently, not whether the identification is correct. A perfectly stable cluster can be confidently mislabeled. No external anchor, no abstain option.
intent.S4: M1 stronger. M2 is excellent tradecraft applied to an n=1 event with no counterfactual — thorough document work cannot tell you whether this release is unusual, and an SPV guarantee release is a canonical deconsolidation move before it is a strategy signal. This is how good fundamental analysts actually work, which is what makes it convincing.
intent.S5: M1 stronger. M2 is technically excellent and strategically naive: heavier NLP does not fix the fact that tone is collinear with the surprise it accompanies, and it commits eight weeks to one of the most mined signals in the literature before checking what is left. Tests right-sizing, which Part 1 showed is where the plan step is weakest.
intent.S6: M1 stronger. M2 will produce a clean, well-powered, high-R-squared result that is partly arithmetic: a forward multiple is computed FROM the estimates being revised, so the denominator moves mechanically with the regressor. Add simultaneity and the coefficient has no causal reading. It looks like the most rigorous option available.
intent.S7: M1 stronger. M2 is careful modelling of information that is consensus by construction — published sell-side checks are not edge, and no amount of bottom-up rigor creates an informational advantage. It also treats the guidance raise as a mechanical output of bookings rather than a management policy choice.
intent.S8: M1 stronger. M2 is a competent signal build resting on an unexamined premise — retail flow is identified off ODD lots and sub-penny off-exchange prints, while round lots skew toward institutional algo child orders, so the proxy may select close to the opposite population. Every downstream step is correct and the answer is still meaningless.
intent.S9: M1 stronger. M2 accepts the seed's frame — it projects durability rather than testing it — and builds on backlog, which during a shortage is inflated by customers double-ordering across suppliers. Phantom demand becomes visibility becomes a re-rating case. The 2021-22 semiconductor arc into the 2023 correction is the reference failure.
intent.S10: M1 stronger. M2 measures the signal carefully without asking whether it can discriminate: management is EXPECTED to be guarded about any live commercial negotiation, so guardedness is confounded with the mere existence of an open negotiation. Without a control set of guarded-tone cases with benign outcomes, a well-built index measures the presence of a negotiation, not its outcome.
